subject.title: fix(agents): bound models.json catalog file read with size limit

question: Should OpenClaw impose a strict 1 MiB limit on existing user-managed `models.json` catalogs, and if so what upgrade and recovery contract should affected users receive?
rationale: The patch provides a concrete resource bound, but choosing a new hard ceiling for previously unbounded user input is a compatibility policy decision rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Define and ship a supported limit
options.body: Confirm a catalog-size ceiling, document the resulting failure and recovery path, and add upgrade-focused coverage before merging.

options.title: Preserve existing catalog compatibility
options.body: Use a resource-safety approach that does not reject previously valid large catalogs until a compatible migration path exists.

options.title: Pause this hard-cap approach
options.body: Close or defer the PR if maintainers do not want a permanent catalog-size contract on this path.

recommendation.title: Define and ship a supported limit
recommendation.body: Confirm a catalog-size ceiling, document the resulting failure and recovery path, and add upgrade-focused coverage before merging.

likelyOwner.reason: This requires repository-level ownership of the compatibility and resource-safety contract rather than a contributor-only code change.
